function: Excluded (above_phy): DDQN selects radar or communication function, message type and rate level from hazard and queue states; ADMM-Net completes missing weather and traffic states (pp. 2, 5-8).
notes: Reason above_phy. PDF title (p. 1) is 'Joint Deep Reinforcement Learning and Unfolding for Sensing and Communication Function Selection in Vehicular Networks' and the DOI printed on p. 1 matches. The learned parts are a DDQN policy that, at each step, activates the radar or the communication function ('a vehicle can selectively activate either the radar or the communication function based on environmental states', p. 2), picks the message type (CAM or DENM) and a rate level (pp. 4, 6), and ADMM-Net, a deep-unfolded matrix completion of missing weather, traffic and ACK states (pp. 7-8: 'we use ADMM-Net to accurately complete the missing environmental states, and then use DDQN to solve the problem'); this is scheduling and environment-state completion above the physical layer. The physical layer is abstracted: the channel is a quality level from 1 to 10 (p. 5: 'it is abstracted as the channel quality level'), the environment variables 'are represented as an abstract hazard level' built from a US accident dataset (p. 9), the radar has two fixed modes (p. 9), and no antenna array, beam, waveform design, RIS or channel estimation appears in the paper's own model. Borderline for the reviewer: if the radar-mode and rate-level choices are counted as physical-layer decisions learned jointly with the scheduling, the work passes above_phy and would then be excluded as function (link adaptation and radar-mode choice are not among the seven areas) or, read as area 5, as system (scalar SINR link, no antenna array or RIS, p. 4). It is excluded in every reading. Quantitative simulation results exist (Figs. 5-9, pp. 10-12), so results is not the reason.
